subject: Post-incident customer briefing: token-generation delay and remediation steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@patternpay.com>, PatternPay Ops <ops@patternpay.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident briefing: token-generation delay and next steps

Hi Elena / PatternPay team,

Thank you again for your patience during the token-generation slowdowns you observed yesterday morning. We finished our investigation and I wanted to share a concise customer-facing summary of what happened, the immediate mitigations we applied, and the concrete actions we are taking to reduce recurrence risk. Please find a short timeline attached (token-delay-timeline.xlsx) and our hotfix notes (hotfix-1.2.3-release-notes.pdf).

Summary of impact
- Window: 2027-07-18 06:20–07:05 UTC (approx).
- Symptom: intermittent multi-second stalls per-token for requests with >8k context; errors were rare but latency spikes caused backpressure in your request queue.
- Scope: ~12% of generation requests routed to the affected runtime pool; elevated p95/p99 token latency for those calls.

Investigation highlights (concise)
- Trigger: a kernel selection regression introduced in our 1.2.2 runtime build that changed the fallback path for attention kernels when KV cache fragmentation occurred.
- Amplifier: a recently deployed prefix-caching policy change increased KV cache churn for long-context workloads, which exposed the regression under production load.
- Outcome: for certain requests, the runtime retried a suboptimal kernel path causing repeated device synchronization and per-token stalls.

Immediate mitigations taken
1) Rolled back the 1.2.2 kernel selection change within 20 minutes of detection, returning affected hosts to the prior stable path.
2) Scoped autoscaling to favor pools with the validated kernel configuration for long-context workloads.
3) Deployed a hotfix (1.2.3) that adds a fast path guard to avoid the fallback loop while we fully remediate the selector logic.

Customer-facing impact: the rollback and hotfix reduced elevated token latency back to baseline within ~30 minutes; we estimate 95% of affected requests returned to normal latency within the first hour after mitigation.

Planned actions and timelines
- Short term (this week): complete e2e validation of 1.2.3 across long-context replay workloads and promote the hotfix to all regions by 2027-07-21 23:59 UTC (owner: Connor O'Brien).
- Mid term (2–3 weeks): refactor kernel selector tests and add a synthetic long-context load test to CI to catch this class of regressions earlier (owner: Karthik Iyer).
- Longer term (60 days): introduce a KV cache fragmentation monitor and automatic routing rule to protect long-context customer routes during cache churn events (owner: Platform Reliability).

Compensation / credits
We understand the impact on your service. I’ll coordinate with our billing team and account lead and follow up with a proposal for a one-time credit within 72 hours.

Attachments: token-delay-timeline.xlsx (timeline & raw p99 plots), hotfix-1.2.3-release-notes.pdf (what changed in the guard).

If you want a short sync to talk through the timeline or the technical mitigation we can schedule a 30-minute call — happy to set that up this week.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-incident briefing: token-generation delay and next steps

Thanks — pushing the validated 1.2.3 build through canary now. A few internal clarifications for the customer note:
- Added measured p50/p95/p99 values to the timeline spreadsheet (sheet: customer-summary) so PatternPay can see before/after curves.
- Confirmed rollback occurred at 06:44 UTC and hotfix gate-open at 07:02 UTC. I included those timestamps in the attachment.
- For the longer-term item, I propose we list JIRA INF-1284 as the tracking ticket for the kernel-selector refactor.

I'll take ownership of the short-term promotion and the canary validation (owner: connor.obrien). ETA for global promotion: 2027-07-21 18:00 UTC if validation is clean.

Connor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

On Mon, 19 Jul 2027 at 09:12, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Elena / PatternPay team,
>
> Thank you again for your patience during the token-generation slowdowns you observed yesterday morning...
From: Elena Morales <elena@patternpay.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: PatternPay Ops <ops@patternpay.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident briefing: token-generation delay and next steps

Thanks, Jasmine and team — this is helpful and clear. A few questions from our ops team:
1) Can you confirm whether any requests were re-sent by Redwood or if the stalls simply delayed responses? Our logs show some client-side retries that may have compounded queueing.
2) For the proposed KV fragmentation monitor, will there be alerts exposed to customer dashboards or only internal alarms? We would prefer a dashboard-level signal if possible.

We are open to a short call. Would 2027-07-20 15:00 UTC work for a 30-minute follow-up to review the timeline and the planned credit?

Elena
Head of Ops, PatternPay
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@patternpay.com>, PatternPay Ops <ops@patternpay.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident briefing: token-generation delay and next steps

Elena — thanks for the quick reply and good questions. Answers below: 
1) Retries: we confirmed no automatic re-sends were issued by Redwood for these requests. The stalls led to delayed responses which in some cases triggered your client-side retry logic. We'll add a brief note to the timeline sheet indicating where customer-side retries appear in the trace to help correlate.
2) KV fragmentation monitoring: initial implementation will be internal (alert to SRE on duty). We will add an exported metric and a simple threshold-based signal to the customer-facing console as part of the mid-term work (target: 2–3 weeks), with a preview dashboard we can share earlier if helpful.

Call confirmed: 2027-07-20 15:00 UTC — I’ll send a calendar invite and include Connor for the technical walkthrough and our account lead for the credit discussion.

Action log (owners & ETAs):
- Promote and validate hotfix 1.2.3 globally (Connor O'Brien) — target 2027-07-21 18:00 UTC.
- Add p50/p95/p99 before/after to timeline and mark client-side retry artifacts (Jasmine Liu) — target 2027-07-20 12:00 UTC.
- Open INF-1284 and start kernel-selector refactor planning (Karthik Iyer) — planning ticket created, backlog grooming next week.
- Billing credit proposal (Account Lead) — deliver within 72 hours.

Thanks again — we’ll follow up after the walk-through with an updated timeline and the credit proposal.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
